witness_description: No witness. The claim is a parenthetical stating two premises about objects S, R_{m-1}, W_m produced by an unstated construction ('by construction R_{m-1} has no edges to W_m'); it quantifies over nothing enumerable, so no finite structure can serve as a counterexample without inventing the missing construction.
refutation_explanation: The claim text supplies only '(since S ⊇ R_{m-1}, and by construction R_{m-1} has no edges to W_m).' Neither S, R_{m-1}, W_m, the graph, nor the index m is defined in the text; premise (P2) explicitly appeals to an absent construction. The fragment asserts properties of specific constructed objects rather than a universally quantified statement, so exhibiting an arbitrary graph and sets violating 'S ⊇ R' or 'no R-W edges' would not refute it. Deciding the claim requires the surrounding construction, which the text does not supply; inventing it is disallowed.
search_space: No refutation search space is determined by the claim. As a documented sanity check only, the program exhaustively swept all 4096 combinations of graphs on 3 labeled vertices (2^3 edge subsets) with all triples (S, R, W) of subsets of the vertex set (8^3), using exact integer/set arithmetic in fixed iteration order, confirming both premises are contingent (P1 satisfied 1728/4096, P2 satisfied 2120/4096) and hence undecidable without the missing construction.
